title: Aurora Finance - Procurement: MSA/DPA/SLA/Onboarding

SE to run a 72-hour SLA/throughput benchmark on Aurora test dataset and share results by 2026-05-28
Pricing team to provide formal quote for 12-month Dedicated commitment by 2026-05-24
Schedule onboarding kickoff (technical) for week of 2026-06-01
action_items: Sofia Patel: Send redlined MSA + DPA (include KMS language) - due 2026-05-22
Marcus Lee: Run benchmark (72-hour) and upload results to shared drive - due 2026-05-28

summary: Procurement and legal review covering MSA/DPA edits, SLA expectations, pricing approval path, and onboarding timeline. Customer requested stronger KMS/HSM language, an explicit data residency clause, and a 72-hour performance run to validate SLA claims before final pricing approval.
topics: MSA redlines and DPA wording (encryption/KMS, data residency)
SLA targets for p99 latency and uptime, penalties/fallbacks
Pricing approvals and committed Dedicated capacity option
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jenna (Redwood CSM); Daniel, Riya, Omar, Maya (Aurora Finance)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro from our side, I'm Sofia, AE on this account, Marcus is our systems engineer, Jenna is your CSM who will support onboarding.
[00:12] Daniel: Thanks. quick note, Riya and Omar are here for legal and infra, Maya is on security. we want to focus on contract changes and SLA before we go to procurement committee.
[00:24] Sofia: Great, that's the plan. Agenda - MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations and benchmarking, pricing/commit path, and next steps for onboarding.
[00:35] Marcus: I'll jump into the technical bits when we talk SLA and benchmarks, but first on MSA/DPA: Sofia, can you summarize what we've already shared?
[00:42] Sofia: Sure. We uploaded our standard MSA and DPA earlier this week, plus the SOC 2 Type II report and our security pack. Riya sent a set of redlines to the DPA yesterday, mostly around encryption key ownership, data residency and deletion timelines.
[00:58] Riya: Right - primary asks: 1) explicit KMS/HSM key custodianship language (we want customer-managed keys for inference logs), 2) data residency clause requiring EU-only processing for any EU customer data, and 3) a 30-day hard-delete timeline for logs unless there's a legal hold.
[01:20] Marcus: Quick clarification - for customer-managed keys we support a KMS integration; we have options for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a bring-your-own-HSM flow for Private deployments. there's some nuance on logs vs. model cache (kv cache) because ephemeral KV caches aren't persisted by default.
[01:40] Omar: That nuance matters. if kv cache or prefix cache gets materialized for debugging, we need to ensure it's encrypted with the customer KMK. Is that supported in Dedicated?
[01:50] Marcus: Yes, Dedicated and Private both can be configured to encrypt logs and persisted artifacts with your KMS. for Hosted we have customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest in some regions, but not all - we'll list supported regions.
[02:05] Maya: Also need encryption-in-transit confirmation and key rotation procedures. we've seen vendors be vague about rotation cadence.
[02:12] Marcus: We rotate service keys quarterly, and customer-managed keys follow whatever rotation you enforce in your KMS. we can add language to the DPA referencing rotation best practices and the ability to provide rotation logs on request.
[02:30] Riya: Good. second point on the DPA - SLA enforcement and remedies. procurement wants clear remedies if we have a breach or SLA miss.
[02:38] Jenna: Understood. on SLAs we typically offer uptime & latency targets for Dedicated commitments. for hosted accounts we have published latency percentiles but SLA-backed guarantees are tied to Dedicated/enterprise plans.
[02:52] Daniel: Aurora is aiming for predictable latency - p99 under 800ms for text-generation endpoints with our typical prompt lengths. is that feasible on a Dedicated pool?
[03:03] Marcus: p99 800ms is within the range for Dedicated with appropriate GPU class and batching config; the test will depend on sequence length and tokens-per-request. part of the benchmark we proposed is to run your representative workload for 72 hours to validate.
[03:20] Omar: For the benchmark we'll provide a 4-hour synthetic run first, then longer. question: if the benchmark fails to meet p99, do we revisit pricing or capacity?
[03:31] Sofia: Good question. from a procurement standpoint our standard is to adjust configs or recommend a different instance class. if SLA isn't met due to our stack, there's a remediation plan and we can discuss credits or a service credit schedule in the SLA. specific financial remedies are negotiable for enterprise deals.
[03:49] Riya: We need that in the MSA - a clear service credit table tied to uptime and response time metrics, not just a generic clause.
[03:57] Marcus: We can supply a proposed service credit schedule. typical benchmarks we've run: for a 12-node Dedicated pool with A100-equivalent instances and optimized batching, p95 around 120ms, p99 around 500-700ms depending on prompt shape. but again, that's workload-dependent; we will run Aurora's test set.
[04:20] Daniel: Ok. Pricing - procurement needs a formal quote with both hosted and Dedicated options, and a committed 12-month discount tier.
[04:29] Sofia: Pricing team will provide that. typical discounts for 12-month reserved capacity start at 20% and increase with higher commits. we'll deliver a quote with three options: self-serve hosted list price, 12-month Dedicated commit baseline, and a hybrid with burst capacity.
[04:45] Riya: We'll need to know termination clauses and how unused committed capacity is handled in the MSA.
[04:52] Sofia: We can include a usage true-up or a credit system. we'll propose flexible commit terms in the redline.
[04:59] Maya: Security - besides SOC2, we need logs retention controls, audit logs, SSO (SAML), RBAC, and a pen test report.
[05:10] Marcus: We have SAML SSO, role-based access controls, and audit event export. pen test reports are available under NDA; we'll attach the summary in the security pack.
[05:22] Riya: Good. also need an explicit data deletion workflow and attestation once data is deleted.
[05:29] Jenna: We can provide deletion attestation for onboarding and for any requested deletes. we'll add process steps in the onboarding checklist.
[05:36] Daniel: Timeline - procurement committee meets next Thursday (2026-05-27). we need redlines and the formal quote before then to get sign-off. can you commit to these dates?
[05:46] Sofia: Yes. commit to send redlined MSA/DPA by Friday 2026-05-22 and pricing quote by Sunday 2026-05-24. Marcus will run the benchmark and share results by 2026-05-28, which is after committee but the committee can provisionally approve based on proposed SLA and waterfall.
[06:02] Omar: For the benchmark we'll need a test account with tokens and a dataset. Omar: I'll send those details to Marcus after this call.
[06:10] Marcus: Thanks - please include sample prompts and sequence length distributions so we can match batching behavior.
[06:17] Riya: A few legal clarifications: do you accept a mutual indemnity clause and can we add a data processing addendum that names subprocessors?
[06:27] Sofia: We accept mutual indemnity with standard carve-outs for open-source and third-party infra, and we can list subprocessors in DPA appendix.
[06:36] Maya: Also need to confirm PCI/NIST/etc applicability; Aurora handles card data upstream and only summaries will hit inference. we need assurance that Redwood won't retain PII beyond the retention window.
[06:48] Marcus: We'll map field-level redaction options and show how to configure prefix caching to avoid storing PII. for any persisted artifacts we can configure masking.
[06:58] Daniel: Onboarding plan - assuming committee approval, we'd like a pilot onboarding of 2 months to validate integration, with a clear success criteria document.
[07:08] Jenna: Our standard pilot includes: 1) sandbox access, 2) 72-hour performance run, 3) integration playbook, and 4) quality/regression checks using your prompt set. we can produce success criteria doc by next Tuesday.
[07:20] Daniel: Can you also include estimated ramp time for switching to Dedicated if pilot is positive?
[07:24] Marcus: Typically 3-6 weeks for Dedicated provisioning and validation depending on region and instance availability. we can provide an accelerated path if you purchase a commit and we reserve capacity in advance.
[07:36] Riya: On DPA wording again - for EU data residency will you accept a clause that processing of EU data happens in EU region only, and subprocessors are EU-based?
[07:47] Sofia: For Dedicated/Private yes. For Hosted we can guarantee EU-region processing in supported regions and list subprocessors by region. we'll reflect this in the DPA appendix and highlight any regions where it's not currently supported.
[07:59] Omar: What about logging retention - 30 days is fine for us, but we'd like a hard-delete option after 30 days unless there's a legal hold clause.
[08:08] Jenna: We'll include a 30-day default retention and a documented legal hold process. deletion attestation will be available upon request.
[08:16] Daniel: Procurement also asked about SLA penalties being capped. they generally accept a cap but want it to be meaningful.
[08:24] Sofia: We typically cap credits at a percentage of monthly fees; we can propose a tiered schedule where major breaches result in larger credits. we'll provide sample numbers in the revised MSA.
[08:35] Riya: Please ensure the MSA includes a clear definition of "downtime" for inference endpoints and method of measurement (synthetic probes vs customer telemetry).
[08:44] Marcus: We'll propose measurement via internal monitoring with cross-checks to your probes; measurements will be averaged over the billing period with clear p99/p95 definitions.
[08:56] Daniel: Quick question on support SLAs - do you offer a named technical account manager for enterprise deals?
[09:02] Sofia: Yes for enterprise we can offer a TAM and 24/7 on-call options as an add-on. we'll include that in the quote.
[09:10] Maya: Last security question - can you commit to annual pen testing and share remediation timelines?
[09:16] Marcus: Annual pen test yes, typical remediation windows are 30-90 days based on severity; critical issues are handled immediately with customer notification.
[09:26] Riya: For the redline process - we'll send DPA redlines in tracked changes and expect Redwood to respond in tracked changes as well.
[09:33] Sofia: That's fine. we'll return a redlined MSA/DPA and mark up any non-starters.
[09:38] Daniel: Ok next, procurement flow. Daniel: Our procurement timeline - procurement committee 2026-05-27, budget approvals by 2026-06-03, legal sign-off by 2026-06-05. if we can meet these dates we can onboard in early June.
[09:54] Sofia: We'll try to meet that cadence. Marcus: for the benchmark, one ask - can we run both hosted and dedicated configurations to compare latency/cost?
[10:02] Marcus: yes we can do both; it helps to justify the commit if dedicated gives 40-60% cost savings on sustained workloads.
[10:10] Omar: On the test environment, can you provide isolated test instances so we don't cross tenant data?
[10:15] Marcus: Absolutely - sandbox accounts are isolated and we can replicate your network constraints if needed for Private deployment testing.
[10:22] Riya: Also need to confirm export controls and compliance for any models that originate from third parties.
[10:28] Sofia: We'll include a section on export compliance in the security pack and list any model licenses or restrictions.
[10:35] Daniel: Any blockers from Redwood's side for the proposed schedule?
[10:39] Sofia: No blockers. we'll commit to the deliverables. Jenna will coordinate onboarding and Marcus will own benchmark execution.
[10:47] Marcus: I'll follow up with a benchmark plan template and the exact test credentials we need.
[10:52] Daniel: Great. Any final questions?
[10:55] Riya: Please include a list of subprocessors and their locations in the DPA appendix.
[10:59] Sofia: Will do.
[11:01] Daniel: Alright, recap and next steps?
[11:04] Sofia: Recap: Redwood sends redlined MSA/DPA by 2026-05-22; pricing quote by 2026-05-24; Marcus runs 72-hour benchmark and shares results by 2026-05-28; Aurora to send test dataset and access by 2026-05-23. procurement committee meets 2026-05-27.
[11:22] Daniel: That works. thanks everyone. we'll look for the redlines and quote.
[11:26] Sofia: Thanks all. we'll follow up in email with links to the security pack and the shared drive for benchmark results.
[11:33] Meeting ended.
